messages:
felix: heads-up — new user running the docker quickstart hit 402 on first API call despite adding a card in the console. they used the provided docker-compose and the sample app logs show the request going out but api returns Payment Required. :thinking:

felix: repro steps (from their terminal):
```bash
# follow quickstart: docker-compose up
# then inside container
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live...\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

felix: response body:
```json
{"error":"payment_required","message":"workspace billing inactive"}
```

anya: org id / user? did they create workspace via the web UI or were they invited into an org? also which quickstart (docker image tag)?

felix: org: org_D3p...r0, user: docker-new@startup.com. They created the workspace, entered card, console showed billing active. Quickstart image: redwood/quickstart:latest (docker flow uses the runtime app which proxies outgoing requests).

onboarding-bot: Workspace org_D3p...r0 created 2026-03-25T09:41:02Z. Billing webhook processed: payment_intent.succeeded. Billing link status: linked -> active.

matt: two things to consider: 1) our quickstart docker uses an outbound webhook/websocket to the console to stream events; if customer network blocks callbacks (corporate firewall), the console may show card but the linking job's callback to internal billing service can fail. 2) the containerized quickstart caches local metadata at startup and may have grabbed a stale org status before the billing link completed.

anya: can you get the container logs? the quickstart image logs the reason when it receives a 402. look for "billing_status=" fields.

felix: logs show: \"startup: fetch org metadata -> status: inactive (cached)\" then later \"payment webhook received\" but no in-process reload. They never restarted the docker container after adding card.

matt: that explains it. the quickstart should poll the org state for a short period on startup (or subscribe to webhook via long-poll) to avoid this edge. For support immediate fix: (a) restart the container after billing shows active; or (b) create a workspace token and inject it into the container env as REDWOOD_API_KEY. workspace token avoids client-side negative-cache because it's provisioned under the billing context.

support-bot: Suggested workaround: restart quickstart container OR run redwoodctl billing reconcile --org org_D3p...r0 to force link confirmation.

felix: support did restart the container and the call returned 200. output from quickstart after restart:
```json
{"id":"resp_42","output":"hi"}
```

anya: we should update the docker quickstart README: after completing billing steps, restart the container if you used the UI. also change the image entrypoint to attempt a short poll for up to 30s if org status==inactive at startup. I'll open a tiny PR.

matt: engineering follow-ups: (1) quickstart docker image patch to poll org status for 30s with exponential backoff, (2) server-side: mark billing link as authoritative and emit a push event to active containers (or at least bump an X-Org-Billing-Version header) so clients can auto-invalidate cached state. file prod bug: DX-boat-231.

felix: filing a support KB note with the restart and workspace-token workaround. user confirmed everything works after restart. closing out here — thanks all :white_check_mark:
